messages:
siva: Heads-up: seeing a wave of ALB target deregistrations in eu-west-1, started ~09:30 UTC. Health checks to nodeIPs are mostly timing out / being reset.

maya: Which target groups? any AZ or nodepool correlation?

siva: tg-frontend-eu and tg-embed-eu. All failing targets are on the gpu-edge-eu-1 pool in az-b.

infra-oncall: ALB access logs show healthcheck GET /healthz -> 502/504 and TCP resets for the node IPs. Example: "2024-10-12T09:31:02Z GET /healthz 504 10.0.2.45"

aj: Any node-level IP churn? ENI events?

siva: Yes, EC2 console shows an ENI detach+attach sequence on several nodes around the same time (likely recoveries). kube-proxy logs from one node: "Detected node IP change 10.0.2.45 -> 10.0.3.12, rebuilding iptables" then errors removing old nat chains.

leila: If iptables/nat rules aren't rebuilt before healthchecks hit the nodeIP, packets can be SNATed/dropped or forwarded to the wrong socket -> 502/504. Conntrack could also have stale entries.

infra-oncall: Ran conntrack dump around the window, saw tons of TIME_WAIT + a bunch of ESTABLISHED entries pointing to older IPs. Seems like port reuse + IP swap creates noise.

aj: Do the pods report readiness failures? Or is this only visible at ALB level?

infra-oncall: Pods stayed Ready (readiness probes passing on localhost). This is host-network/hostPort path problem: ALB -> nodeIP:targetPort sometimes never reaches the kube-proxy/iptables chain correctly.

leila: Short-term mitigation: increase TG unhealthy threshold and set deregistration_delay to 120s to avoid flapping during ENI churn. Also recommend forcing kube-proxy to rebuild rules on the pool (roll the DS).

maya: Agree. Any minimal steps we can take now?

infra-oncall: Actions taken: 1) bumped unhealthy threshold from 2 -> 5, deregistration delay -> 120s on tg-frontend-eu and tg-embed-eu. 2) restarted kube-proxy daemonset on gpu-edge-eu-1 nodes one at a time.

deploy-bot: autoscaler detected replacement: node-replacement started for gpu-edge-eu-1-azb (i-0a1b2c3).

siva: After kube-proxy restarts the healthchecks mostly stabilized and targets re-registered. Still want a follow-up to prevent recurrence.

aj: Long-term options: 1) migrate critical TGs to IP mode (targets = podIPs) if we can enable pod ENIs or CNI IP-per-pod; 2) use NLB + proxy protocol to hit sidecar/pod rather than nodeIP; 3) investigate preserving source IP / IP persisting on ENI failover. Need cost/ops tradeoffs.

maya: Please create a follow-up ticket to evaluate IP-mode TG vs NLB vs CNI changes, include expected ops complexity and cost.

leila: I'll draft a short playbook: run conntrack dump, inspect kube-proxy logs, restart kube-proxy DS, temporarily raise TG thresholds, and validate post-restart.

siva: Thanks. I'll write notes into the incident doc and link to this thread. Ping #incidents if it recurs.

infra-oncall: marking incident as mitigated for now, monitoring for 30m.
